To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the productivity of a murine hybridoma can be improved by adaptation to low serum and that this adaptation is accompanied by the appearance of low antibody-producing cells.

(1) the productivity of the antibody 167.4G3.3 is diminished during adaptation to low serum (1-2%) and to serum-free conditions, and (2) the loss of productivity during adaptation can be attributed to the presence of two cell subpopulations, with low and high antibody productivity, respectively.

1) the loss of antibody production in hybridoma cells is due to the appearance of low antibody-producing cells; 2) this phenomenon occurs during adaptation from high to low serum concentration; and 3) the loss of productivity can be avoided if the cells remain in a high serum environment.

the loss of antibody production during the adaptation of a hybridoma line to low serum and serum free culture conditions.
the development of serum-free media for the production of monoclonal antibodies.
